computePromptContentHash() only hashed the system prompt text, not the TASK/RESPONSE_REQUIREMENTS fixed strings, the runtime message template, the untrusted-data delimiters, the structural field selection, or CONTEXT_SCHEMA_VERSION. A developer could have changed any of those without the hash changing, without a version bump, and without any test failing. Verified empirically: a TASK-text-only change was NOT caught by the old hash function (confirmed by reasoning about its implementation) and IS caught by the new one (confirmed by temporarily perturbing advisor-system.ts's TASK text and observing the test fail, then reverting). Fixed in lib/stella/prompts/prompt-content-hash.ts; all 6 expectedContentHash values in registry.ts recomputed; version numbers NOT bumped (the prompts' actual wording did not change, only what the control measures).

Regression introduced while fixing STL-A16-003, caught by pnpm test:unit: audit-log.ts's recordStellaInteraction() called computePromptContentHash(role) at runtime on every interaction, which now internally calls the real buildXUserMessage functions. Under the 4 Stella action test files' mocks (buildXUserMessage mocked to return a plain placeholder string, not a TASK/UNTRUSTED_PROJECT_DATA/RESPONSE_REQUIREMENTS-shaped message), the contract-extraction logic threw, causing 27 test failures across advisor/composer/validator action tests (ok:false instead of ok:true). Root cause: recomputing this hash per-call was unnecessary — it never varies within a prompt-template version. Fixed by using the registry's own recorded snapshot (template.expectedContentHash) at insert time instead of recomputing. All 1277 project-wide unit tests and 49 integration tests pass after the fix.
